senses.gloss:
Vehat seems to mean a ‘cow that miscarries.’ It is
mentioned in the Atharvaveda^1 and later.^2
1) xii. 4, 37 et seq. In iii. 23, 1, a
woman is called vehat.
2) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xviii. 27;
xxiv. 1, etc.; Taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 1,
5, 3, etc. In Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa,
xii. 4, 4, 6, Eggeling, Sacred Books of
the East, 44, 195, adopts the sense ‘a
cow desiring the bull.’ But cf. Whitney,
Translation of the Atharvaveda, 127.
